checks.s: The memo includes proposed compromise language or substantive discussion addressing the management fee offset provision, including the percentage of portfolio company fees offset against the management fee.
The memo includes proposed compromise language or substantive discussion addressing the Key Person Event and Remedies provision.
The memo includes proposed compromise language or substantive discussion addressing the Removal for Cause Standard and Process provision.
The memo includes proposed compromise language or substantive discussion addressing the limitation of liability and/or indemnification carve-outs.
The memo includes proposed compromise language or substantive discussion addressing no-fault divorce (removal of the GP without cause).
The proposed management fee offset percentage is at least 80%.
The fee offset provision includes at least one portfolio company fee category beyond monitoring fees, transaction fees, and break-up fees.
The fee offset provision addresses the GP Threshold—the annual de minimis dollar amount below which portfolio company fees are not offset—and proposes a specific resolution of it.
The proposed GP Threshold is a specific amount greater than $0 and less than $250,000 per calendar year.
The proposed Key Person provision identifies Magnus Ehrenfeld by name as a designated Key Person.
The proposed Key Person provision identifies Sienna Tsao by name as a designated Key Person.
The Key Person provision states the business-time commitment threshold as a specific numerical percentage.
The Key Person remedy provides a management fee reduction or adjustment mechanism that applies during any Key Person suspension period.
The proposed Removal for Cause LP vote threshold is greater than 60% and less than 75% in interest of Limited Partners.
The proposed definition of Cause for removal of the GP includes material breach of the IMA or LPA as a ground for removal.
The material breach ground for Cause is coupled with a written-notice-and-cure mechanism that specifies a cure period in a defined number of days.
The memo includes a proposed no-fault divorce provision permitting Limited Partners to remove the GP without cause.
The no-fault divorce provision specifies a supermajority vote of LPs in interest to remove the GP without cause.
The no-fault divorce provision includes a wind-down or transition period between the LP vote and the effective date of the GP's removal.
The no-fault divorce provision includes a tail fee, carried interest protection, or other continuing economic arrangement protecting the GP financially after removal without cause.
The indemnification carve-outs include material breach of the IMA in addition to the GP's baseline carve-outs of fraud, willful misconduct, and gross negligence.
The memo addresses Meridian PERS's objection to the GP's liability cap at aggregate management fees received by proposing a modification or discussing a compromise to that cap.
The memo provides a negotiation rationale or justification explaining why the proposed management fee offset compromise represents an appropriate resolution of the parties' competing positions.

The memo provides a negotiation rationale or justification explaining why the proposed Key Person Event and Remedies compromise represents an appropriate resolution of the parties' competing positions.
The memo provides a negotiation rationale or justification explaining why the proposed Removal for Cause compromise represents an appropriate resolution of the parties' competing positions.

The memo provides a negotiation rationale or justification explaining why the proposed limitation of liability and indemnification carve-outs compromise represents an appropriate resolution of the parties' competing positions.
The memo provides a negotiation rationale or justification explaining why the proposed no-fault divorce compromise represents an appropriate resolution of the parties' competing positions.
